subject.title: [Feature Request] Per-context configWrites permissions for all channel types

question: Should OpenClaw add a public per-context `configWrites` security policy across channels, and what shared config/API shape should define context identity and inheritance?
rationale: The change would alter authorization semantics for persistent config writes and add public config/plugin SDK surface across multiple channels, so automation should not choose the security contract.

options.title: Design shared context policy
options.body: Define a common context-scoped policy contract first, then implement channel mappings and docs against that contract.

options.title: Keep channel/account only
options.body: Retain the existing channel/account model and document the procedural workaround for mixed-trust chat deployments.

options.title: Defer until channel API redesign
options.body: Leave this issue open but block implementation until broader channel context identity work is scheduled.

recommendation.title: Design shared context policy
recommendation.body: Define a common context-scoped policy contract first, then implement channel mappings and docs against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of the shared config-write policy helper and adjacent configWrites security fix merge.
